abstract: ui-ux.agency is a UX agency Denver startups and software companies hire remotely to design artificial intelligence (AI) features, software as a service (SaaS) products and minimum viable products (MVPs). ui-ux.agency has no Denver office; its only office is in Reston, Virginia. sections.h2: What can a UX agency Denver teams hire remotely design?
sections.answer: Our designers shape the user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) of AI features, SaaS products and startup MVPs, from research and flows to a tested clickable prototype. Your engineers build from those files, and we stay through the build to answer their questions.
sections.body: As a remote design team, we keep every file in Figma and walk through it on video calls across the 2-hour gap. Typical work: an AI copilot inside an existing app, a support chatbot, SaaS onboarding that lifts activation, or a seed-stage MVP. ui-ux.agency is the design team of tkxel, so designs are checked for build effort, and we have designed 200+ products since 2017. Start with AI product design or SaaS product design.

sections.answer: Denver's tech talent pool is one of North America's larger ones: CBRE's 2025 Scoring Tech Talent report counted 116,970 tech specialists, the 13th largest market it measured. Each card below gives a sourced figure and its year.

items.title: Talent pool and pay
items.body: CBRE ranked Denver 14th overall in 2025, with tech at 6.8% of local employment against a 5.3% average for the top 50 markets; the 2026 edition placed it 16th. sections.h2: How does Colorado's new AI law change AI product design?
sections.answer: From January 1, 2027, Colorado's SB 26-189 turns four duties into interface work: notice, an explanation after an adverse outcome, human review and data correction. The table maps each duty to the screen and design deliverable it needs. This is design guidance, not legal advice; confirm scope with counsel.
sections.caption: SB 26-189 duties and the screens they need
rows: Nothing on screen yet. The law covers automated decision-making technology that materially influences consequential decisions, such as employment, housing, lending or insurance.
An inventory of the AI features that shape those decisions, often the first output of an AI product discovery workshop.
A clear disclosure, before the automated tool is used, that it will shape the decision.
A notice pattern and its copy for each decision point.
A plain-language explanation of the tool's role within 30 days, on screen or by email.
An explanation template the team fills for each adverse outcome.
After an adverse outcome, a way to request meaningful human review and reconsideration, which the law requires to the extent commercially reasonable.
A human-review request flow with status tracking, plus an admin queue for reviewers.
A form to correct factually incorrect personal data the tool used.
A correction flow linked to the record behind the decision.
An audit-log field spec for engineers.
Human-review instructions and screens for the documentation a developer gives deployers.

sections.h2: How does a UX agency Denver founders hire remotely run a project?
sections.answer: Our remote projects move through 4 steps, from kickoff to build support, and a tested prototype comes before any code. Each step ends with a file your engineers can use, shared in Figma or FigJam.

items.title: Kickoff and discovery (1–2 weeks)
items.body: Video interviews and an analytics review; for AI products, a ranking of use cases by user value, data readiness and risk.

items.title: Flows and wireframes (1–4 weeks)
items.body: User flows and wireframes start with the riskiest path, often SaaS onboarding or the human-review step of an AI feature.

items.title: Prototype and test (1–3 weeks)
items.body: Usability testing puts the clickable prototype before 5 to 8 real users in Maze or on video calls, with real or recorded large language model (LLM) output for AI features.

items.title: Handoff and build support (1–4 weeks)
items.body: Specs and components live in Figma; our designers sit in on sprint reviews and compare each built screen with the file.

sections.h2: How do Mountain Time and Eastern Time working hours overlap?
sections.answer: Denver, on Mountain Time, runs 2 hours behind Eastern Time all year, so a Denver morning meets an East Coast midday. Every dedicated designer overlaps at least 4 hours with US Eastern time, and many teams choose full overlap. If those 4 hours run 9 a.m.–1 p.m. ET, only 9–11 a.m. falls inside a 9-to-5 Denver day, so agree the shared hours first; the example table shows how the clocks line up.

sections.answer: Short answers to what Denver and Boulder product teams ask before they hire a remote design partner.

faqs.q: What does UX design Denver teams outsource usually cost?
faqs.a: Our published ranges start at $8,000 for a one-week AI discovery workshop and reach $200,000 for a large SaaS product redesign. MVP design runs $15,000–$50,000, and the UI UX design cost guide lists what moves each price.

faqs.q: Can we hire one UX designer Denver teams can add to their sprints?
faqs.a: Yes. A single dedicated designer is possible, with a weekly design-lead review. Teams of 2 to 5 designers cost $15,000–$40,000 per month, and plans run month to month with 30 days notice.

faqs.q: Do you design AI features for Colorado's SB 26-189?
faqs.a: Yes. We design the notice, explanation and correction flows the law describes, plus the request path for an AI feature that needs human review, then test them with users. Signed on May 14, 2026, the law replaced SB 24-205, whose duties never took effect. The Colorado Attorney General enforces it, but under an April 27, 2026 federal court order in xAI v. Weiser, the office will not start enforcement until its rules are final and the court rules on a preliminary injunction. Your counsel confirms whether a feature is covered.

faqs.q: Does the Colorado Privacy Act affect our consent screens?
faqs.a: Yes, if your company meets one of its thresholds, such as processing personal data of 100,000 or more Colorado consumers in a calendar year; its biometric-data rules apply regardless of size. The law has applied since July 1, 2023, and gives people rights to access, correct and delete their data, so consent and data-request screens belong in the design.

faqs.q: Can your designers join our sprint reviews from another time zone?
faqs.a: Yes. Our designers join sprint reviews and compare built screens with the Figma design, in hours your team shares with them. Denver and the Eastern zone change clocks on the same dates, next on November 1, 2026, so the 2-hour gap stays the same in working hours all year.

faqs.q: When can designers start on a Denver startup's product?
faqs.a: Dedicated designers start within 1 to 2 weeks of the first call. For a new AI feature, the AI product discovery workshop then fills the first 1 to 2 weeks and ends with a tested concept and a scoped plan.
